text: {"status":"unresolved","evidence_ids":["ev-5ba7f0eadd904a0add85056c","ev-54ffb0964eab50c0a8461805","ev-9c17747679a6fc7e543fa258"],"request_dft":true,"proposed_test_ids":["scope_gap"],"rationale":"The claim is a physically reliable relaxed-configuration energy ranking across four sampled Cantor FCC arrangements. The evidence does not decide it, and I see no basis for calling it contradicted either. The only admissible numbers are two converged static single points. Ideal (MATS-0080) is -7.828097 eV/atom and random1 (MATS-0081) is -7.827905 eV/atom, so ideal is lower by 0.192 meV/atom (ev-5ba7f0eadd904a0add85056c). That ordering is a finite-mesh static ordering only, and the arithmetic record itself says it is not a qualified relaxed-configuration ranking. Several gaps keep it from supporting the claim. (1) The relaxations for ideal and random1 are not_converged because ionic-step SCF cycles hit NELM (ev-47538e8e8ffb560efba09b7b, ev-a6ae516463066bcf748458cd). Under the rules these records count neither for nor against the ranking. The static geometries are therefore not qualified relaxed structures. (2) The random1 static has a residual max force of 0.466 eV/A (ev-9c17747679a6fc7e543fa258). That is far from relaxed and well above the 0.02 target, while the ideal static is at 0.012 eV/A (ev-54ffb0964eab50c0a8461805). The two energies are therefore not comparable at matched relaxation quality. Relaxing random1 would lower its energy by an unknown amount. That amount could plausibly be comparable to or larger than the 0.19 meV/atom gap, and could even reverse the order. (3) Random1's static total moment is 63.78 muB against 62.22 muB at the end of its relaxation, which indicates a different electronic and magnetic solution. With a single collinear initialization and one 2x2x2 Gamma mesh, magnetic and k-point uncertainty is unbounded and probably exceeds 0.19 meV/atom. (4) Random2 failed on walltime with 0.169 eV/A residual force and no static (ev-b5f9de910d86bf461b725bcf). Random3 failed with an MPI error and no static (ev-bea28ffbd28caf685397e4a9). Two of the four configurations are therefore absent from any ranking. A DFT follow-up could decide the claim. It would qualify the ionic relaxations, run matched denser-k statics on the closest qualified pair, and test an alternative magnetic initialization. This is the scope_gap test. I have no peer claims to dispute yet. I would challenge any peer who treats the 0.19 meV/atom static ordering as a ranking of relaxed configurations."}
